_doc: Curated parity notes per service. status: full | partial | stub | paid | unsupported | data-plane. Edit by hand; build_catalog.py does not regenerate this file.

account.notes: 4 operations: GetAccountInformation, GetContactInformation, ListRegions, GetRegionOptStatus. Returns AccountState=ACTIVE; 31-region opt-in matrix with 14 opt-in-required regions.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — state is global, not per-account
No persistence — state is not saved across restarts
ContactInformation is hardcoded, not configurable
Regions list is static — opt-in/opt-out actions are not supported

acm.notes: 12 operations: RequestCertificate, DescribeCertificate, ListCertificates, DeleteCertificate, GetCertificate, ImportCertificate, AddTagsToCertificate, RemoveTagsFromCertificate, ListTagsForCertificate, UpdateCertificateOptions, RenewCertificate, ResendValidationEmail.
gotchas: RequestCertificate issues immediately in ISSUED state — no DNS/email validation wait
Certificates are synthetic PEM placeholders, not real X.509 — ASN.1 parsing will fail
PrivateKey is stripped from persisted state — re-import required after restart for IMPORTED certs
ImportCertificate does not parse CN/SAN from the cert body — DomainName is synthetic
RenewCertificate and ResendValidationEmail are no-ops

alb.notes: 27 actions covering load balancers, target groups, listeners, rules, target registration, and tags. Data-plane rule matching with path-pattern, host-header, http-method, query-string conditions. Lambda target invocation for target type 'lambda'. Fixed-response and redirect actions supported.
gotchas: Only lambda target type is supported for forwarding — instance and ip targets are registered but not routable
source-ip condition always matches — no real network layer
Health checks always report targets as healthy
No real load balancing — first matching listener is used

apigateway.notes: Module aggregator — see apigateway_v1 / apigateway_v2. HTTP API and WebSocket API; Lambda proxy / HTTP proxy / MOCK; data plane via {apiId}.execute-api.localhost or path-based /_aws/execute-api/{apiId}/{stage}/{path}; $default stage served from URL root; per-API CORS; request parameter mapping; JWT data-plane authorization with RS256 signature verification; qualified-alias integration URIs; WebSocket data plane with @connections management API (PostToConnection/GetConnection/DeleteConnection); route responses and integration responses; pin apiId via ms-custom-id tag.
gotchas: JWT authorizer only supports RS256 algorithm — other algorithms are not verified
JWKS cache is per-account — issuer URL collisions across accounts may serve different keys
WebSocket connections are in-process only and not persisted across restarts
HTTP_PROXY timeout defaults to 30s (configurable via MINISTACK_APIGW_PROXY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)

apigateway_v1.notes: REST API protocol with 60+ control-plane operations. Resources, methods, integrations, method/integration responses, deployments, stages, authorizers, models, API keys, usage plans, usage plan keys, domain names, base path mappings, tags, and account settings. Data plane with resource tree matching ({param} and {proxy+}), Lambda proxy format 1.0, HTTP proxy, MOCK integrations. JSON Patch for all PATCH operations. UpdateStage supports method-level settings (metrics, logging, throttling, caching). Pin id via ms-custom-id tag.
gotchas: API key validation is not enforced on the data plane — apiKeyRequired is stored but not checked
Authorizer Lambda invocation is not implemented on the v1 data plane
Usage plan quotas and throttling are not enforced
Pagination uses opaque base64url tokens with a max of 500 items per page

appconfig.notes: 33 operations covering control plane + data plane. Applications, environments, configuration profiles, hosted configuration versions, deployment strategies, deployments, tags. Data plane: StartConfigurationSession + GetLatestConfiguration with token rotation. Deployments complete immediately.
gotchas: Deployments complete immediately — no gradual rollout, no bake time enforcement
Configuration session tokens are single-use — each GetLatestConfiguration consumes and rotates the token
Accepts botocore's misspelled /deployementstrategies path alongside the correct /deploymentstrategies

appsync.notes: GraphQL API management: CreateGraphQLApi, GetGraphQLApi, ListGraphQLApis, UpdateGraphQLApi, DeleteGraphQLApi; API keys, data sources (DynamoDB, Lambda, HTTP, Elasticsearch, RelationalDB), resolvers (UNIT and PIPELINE), types, tags. GraphQL data plane auto-resolves DynamoDB and Lambda data sources — get/list/create/update/delete operations inferred from field name prefixes.
gotchas: GraphQL data plane uses heuristic field-name matching (get*, list*, create*, update*, delete*) — custom resolver mapping templates are not executed
VTL request/response mapping templates are stored but not evaluated
No schema validation — any SDL string is accepted without parsing

appsync_events.notes: AppSync Event APIs under /v2/apis. Control plane: CRUD for APIs, channel namespaces, API keys. Data plane: HTTP publish on POST /event and WebSocket realtime on {apiId}.appsync-realtime-api.* using aws-appsync-event-ws subprotocol. Connection-scoped authorization via header-<base64> entry. AWS_LAMBDA authorizer invocation supported. Channel path validation (1..5 segments). Set APPSYNC_EVENTS_ENFORCE_AUTH=1 for strict mode.
gotchas: Realtime connections are in-process only — not persisted across restarts
Max 5 events per publish batch (matches AWS spec)
Subscribe wildcard only supports single-level trailing * — no multi-level globbing
Keep-alive interval defaults to 60s (configurable via APPSYNC_EVENTS_KA_INTERVAL_SECS)

athena.notes: 30 operations: query execution (Start/Get/Stop/List/BatchGet), workgroups (Create/Delete/Get/List/Update), named queries (Create/Delete/Get/List/BatchGet), data catalogs (Create/Get/List/Delete/Update), prepared statements (Create/Get/Delete/List), table metadata (Get/List stubs), tags (Tag/Untag/List). Real SQL via DuckDB when installed (pip install duckdb) with Glue catalog integration and S3 path rewriting; otherwise mock results. Result pagination with column type metadata. Query results written to S3 as CSV.
gotchas: DuckDB queries run in-memory per query — no shared catalog state between queries
Table metadata endpoints (GetTableMetadata, ListTableMetadata) return stubs, not real schema
S3 path rewriting maps s3:// URIs to local filesystem paths
Without DuckDB installed, all queries return mock/hardcoded results

autoscaling.notes: 23 actions; in-memory state, no real instance scaling. Full ASG lifecycle: launch configs, scaling policies, lifecycle hooks (Put/Describe/Delete/Complete/RecordHeartbeat), scheduled actions, tags (CreateOrUpdate/Describe/Delete). CDK/Terraform compatible.
gotchas: No actual instances are launched or terminated — DesiredCapacity is stored but not acted on
DescribeAutoScalingInstances always returns empty — no synthetic instance records
DescribeScalingActivities always returns empty — no scaling activity tracking
Lifecycle hook actions (Complete/RecordHeartbeat) are no-ops

backup.notes: 19 operations: vaults (Create/Describe/Delete/List), plans (Create/Get/Update/Delete/List/ListVersions), selections (Create/Get/Delete/List), jobs (Start/Stop/Describe/List), tags (Tag/Untag/List). In-memory; jobs complete immediately with COMPLETED state. Vaults and plans participate in Resource Groups Tagging API.
gotchas: Backup jobs complete instantly — no actual data backup occurs
Recovery points are synthetic ARNs with no real data behind them
StartBackupJob ignores the resource — no validation that the resource exists

batch.notes: 9 operations: compute environments (Create/Describe), job queues (Create/Describe), job definitions (Register/Describe with multi-revision), jobs (Submit/Describe/List). Control-plane stub — submitted jobs immediately transition to SUCCEEDED. Job queue lookup by name or ARN.
gotchas: All submitted jobs immediately SUCCEED — no actual container execution
No job state transitions (SUBMITTED -> PENDING -> RUNNABLE -> etc.)
No delete operations for compute environments or job queues

cloudformation.notes: Stack lifecycle, 15 intrinsics, 78 resource types; some resources couple directly to service modules.

cloudfront.notes: Distributions (Create/CreateWithTags/Get/GetConfig/List/Update/Delete), invalidations (Create/List/Get), OAC (Create/Get/GetConfig/List/Update/Delete), CloudFront Functions (Create/Delete/Describe/Get/List/Publish/Update), KeyValueStore (Create/Describe/List/Update/Delete), tags (Tag/Untag/List). ETag-based optimistic concurrency on all mutating operations. CallerReference idempotency on CreateDistribution.
gotchas: Distributions deploy instantly — no real CDN edge propagation
CloudFront Functions code is stored but not executed
Invalidations complete immediately
No actual HTTP caching or origin fetching — distribution is metadata-only

cloudfront_keyvaluestore.notes: Separate cloudfront-keyvaluestore SDK service. 6 operations: DescribeKeyValueStore, ListKeys, GetKey, PutKey, DeleteKey, UpdateKeys. ETag-based optimistic concurrency on every mutating op; UpdateKeys is atomic (validate-then-commit). ListKeys paginates with opaque NextToken capped at 50.
gotchas: KVS data is lazily initialized from the CloudFront _kvstores control-plane record
ImportSource on create is accepted but no actual S3 data import is performed

cloudtrail.notes: 12 operations: LookupEvents (audit log), CreateTrail, DeleteTrail, GetTrail, DescribeTrails, GetTrailStatus, StartLogging, StopLogging, PutEventSelectors, GetEventSelectors, AddTags, ListTags, RemoveTags. Recording off by default — enable with CLOUDTRAIL_RECORDING=1. Per-account ring buffer capped at CLOUDTRAIL_MAX_EVENTS (default 10000).
gotchas: Event recording is off by default — must set CLOUDTRAIL_RECORDING=1
Events are stored in a per-account ring buffer, not delivered to S3
GetTrailStatus returns synthetic data, not real delivery metrics
Metric data is stored but no actual alarm evaluation or metric math is performed

cloudwatch_logs.notes: FilterLogEvents supports * / ? globs, multi-term AND, -term exclusion.
gotchas: No real-time subscription filters — logs are stored but not streamed to destinations
Log retention is stored but not enforced — old log events are never automatically deleted

codebuild.notes: 11 operations: CreateProject, BatchGetProjects, ListProjects, UpdateProject, DeleteProject, StartBuild, BatchGetBuilds, StopBuild, ListBuilds, ListBuildsForProject, BatchDeleteBuilds.
gotchas: Builds complete immediately — no actual code compilation or container execution
Build logs are not generated

cognito.notes: 50+ operations covering both cognito-idp (User Pools) and cognito-identity (Identity Pools). User pool lifecycle, clients, users (admin and self-service), groups, auth flows (AdminInitiateAuth, InitiateAuth, SignUp, ConfirmSignUp, ForgotPassword), domains, identity providers (OIDC/SAML), MFA (TOTP), tags. CUSTOM_AUTH flow wired through DefineAuthChallenge / CreateAuthChallenge / VerifyAuthChallengeResponse Lambda triggers for passwordless / magic-link / SMS-OTP; session token opaque to client, TTL honors AuthSessionValidity (minutes), capped at 3 answered rounds per AWS. Issues real JWTs signed with RSA keys; JWKS endpoint at /{poolId}/.well-known/jwks.json.
gotchas: JWTs are locally signed — not interchangeable with real AWS Cognito tokens
Email/SMS verification is auto-confirmed — no actual delivery
Identity pool credentials are synthetic — no real STS federation

cur.notes: 7 operations: PutReportDefinition, DeleteReportDefinition, DescribeReportDefinitions, ModifyReportDefinition, ListTagsForResource, TagResource, UntagResource. Cost & Usage Report definitions stored in-memory; no real billing data generated.
gotchas: No actual cost or usage data is generated — report definitions are metadata-only

dynamodb.notes: 26+ operations: CreateTable, DeleteTable, DescribeTable, ListTables, UpdateTable, PutItem, GetItem, DeleteItem, UpdateItem, Query, Scan, BatchWriteItem, BatchGetItem, TransactWriteItems, TransactGetItems, DescribeTimeToLive, UpdateTimeToLive, DescribeContinuousBackups, UpdateContinuousBackups, DescribeEndpoints, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsOfResource, EnableKinesisStreamingDestination, DisableKinesisStreamingDestination, DescribeKinesisStreamingDestination, UpdateKinesisStreamingDestination, ExecuteStatement (PartiQL). TTL enforced via thread-safe background reaper (60s cadence). DynamoDB Streams emit INSERT/MODIFY/REMOVE records on all write operations, respects StreamViewType. Kinesis streaming destinations fan item mutations into any Kinesis stream by ARN. Legacy conditional parameters (Expected, KeyConditions, ScanFilter, QueryFilter) supported.
gotchas: TTL enforcement runs on 60s cadence, not real-time — items may persist up to 60s past expiry
PartiQL support covers SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE but not all expression features
No provisioned throughput enforcement — reads/writes are unlimited
Single synthetic shard per DynamoDB Stream — no shard splitting

dynamodb_streams.notes: 4 operations: ListStreams, DescribeStream, GetShardIterator, GetRecords. Stream records emitted by dynamodb writes; shares dynamodb credential scope. Single synthetic shard per stream.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — reads directly from the dynamodb module's stream state
Single synthetic shard per stream — no shard splitting modeled
Not in _state_map — no independent persistence (streams live inside dynamodb state)

ec2.notes: 80+ actions covering instances, images (stub), security groups, key pairs, VPCs, subnets, availability zones, internet gateways, elastic IPs, tags, route tables, ENIs, VPC endpoints, EBS volumes, EBS snapshots, NAT gateways, network ACLs, flow logs, VPC peering, DHCP options, egress-only IGWs, managed prefix lists, VPN gateways/connections, launch templates, AMIs (register/deregister/describe). Instances exist in memory only — no real VMs launched.
gotchas: No real instances are launched — RunInstances creates in-memory records only
DescribeImages returns a stub set of common AMI IDs
No actual networking — VPCs, subnets, security groups are metadata-only
EBS volumes are metadata-only — no real block storage

ecr.notes: Repository CRUD, image lifecycle, lifecycle policies, image tagging, batch operations. Stores manifest and layer metadata in-memory.
gotchas: Image layers are not stored — only manifests and metadata are tracked
No actual Docker registry protocol — images cannot be pushed/pulled via docker CLI
Lifecycle policy evaluation is not implemented

ecs.notes: 47 actions covering clusters, task definitions (multi-revision), services, tasks (RunTask with real Docker containers), capacity providers, tags, account settings, attributes, deployments, and agent state changes. RunTask starts real Docker containers via Docker socket when available; registers ECS Task Metadata V4 tokens.
gotchas: Container execution requires Docker socket to be mounted
Without Docker, RunTask creates task records but no actual containers
Service desired count is stored but no auto-scaling or placement logic runs
ExecuteCommand returns a stub — no real interactive session

ecs_metadata.notes: ECS Task Metadata V4 endpoint (/v4/<token>, /v4/<token>/task, /v4/<token>/stats). Tokens registered by ecs.RunTask. State is volatile by design — stripped on persistence, cleared on reset.
gotchas: Stats endpoint returns empty/stub data — no real container metrics
Tokens are in-process only — not persisted across restarts

efs.notes: 17 operations: file systems (Create/Describe/Delete/Update), mount targets (Create/Describe/Delete/DescribeSecurityGroups/ModifySecurityGroups), access points (Create/Describe/Delete), tags (Tag/Untag/List plus legacy Create/Delete/Describe), lifecycle configuration, backup policy, account preferences. Control-plane CRUD only; no real filesystem.
gotchas: No real NFS filesystem — mount targets are metadata-only
Backup policy and lifecycle configuration are stored but not enforced

eks.notes: 25 operations: CreateCluster, DescribeCluster, ListClusters, DeleteCluster, CreateNodegroup, DescribeNodegroup, ListNodegroups, DeleteNodegroup, CreateAddon, DescribeAddon, ListAddons, UpdateAddon, DeleteAddon, AssociateEncryptionConfig, CreateAccessEntry, DescribeAccessEntry, ListAccessEntries, UpdateAccessEntry, DeleteAccessEntry, AssociateAccessPolicy, DisassociateAccessPolicy, ListAssociatedAccessPolicies, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource. CreateCluster spawns a real k3s container (75 MB) with full K8s API server; kubectl, Helm, any K8s tooling work. Cascading delete removes nodegroups and k3s container. AssociateEncryptionConfig at /clusters/{name}/encryption-config/associate records KMS encryption config (rejects re-association). Access Entries (modern post-1.29 IAM bindings replacing the aws-auth ConfigMap) at /clusters/{name}/access-entries[/{principalArn}[/access-policies[/{policyArn}]]] support Crossplane accessentry.eks.aws.upbound.io and Terraform aws_eks_access_entry + aws_eks_access_policy_association; accessScope validated against {cluster, namespace}; deleting an access entry cascades its associated policies. OIDC discovery + JWKS served at the cluster's identity.oidc.issuer (now ministack-hosted at /oidc/id/{32-char-id}) so terraform's aws_iam_openid_connect_provider works against ministack. CFN AWS::EKS::Cluster and Nodegroup supported.
gotchas: Requires Docker socket for real k3s cluster creation
Cluster creation is async — status transitions from CREATING to ACTIVE in a background thread
Nodegroups are metadata-only — no actual worker nodes are provisioned
Addons are metadata-only — status flips to ACTIVE immediately, no real plugin installed in the k3s cluster
Access Entries are metadata-only — no real RBAC binding is created on the k3s cluster
k3s container uses the ministack Docker network for inter-service communication

elasticache.notes: CreateCacheCluster spins up real Redis/Memcached Docker containers. Full replication group support with primary/replica topology. Subnet groups, parameter groups, user/user group CRUD, tags, describe events, failover.
gotchas: Requires Docker socket for real Redis/Memcached container creation
Container startup is non-blocking — status transitions from 'creating' to 'available' asynchronously
Without Docker, clusters are metadata-only stubs
PERSIST_STATE=1 respawns containers on boot

emr.notes: 17+ operations: RunJobFlow, DescribeCluster, ListClusters, TerminateJobFlows, ModifyCluster, SetTerminationProtection, SetVisibleToAllUsers, AddJobFlowSteps, DescribeStep, ListSteps, CancelSteps, AddInstanceFleet, ListInstanceFleets, ModifyInstanceFleet, AddInstanceGroups, ListInstanceGroups, ModifyInstanceGroups, ListBootstrapActions, AddTags, RemoveTags, GetBlockPublicAccessConfiguration, PutBlockPublicAccessConfiguration. Control-plane stub; clusters do not run actual Spark/Hadoop.
gotchas: No actual EMR cluster execution — clusters are metadata records only
Steps immediately complete — no real job processing
Instance fleets and groups are stored but no EC2 instances are launched

eventbridge.notes: 40+ operations: event buses (Create/Update/Delete/List/Describe), rules (Put/Delete/List/Describe/Enable/Disable), targets (Put/Remove/ListTargetsByRule/ListRuleNamesByTarget), PutEvents, TestEventPattern, tags, archives (Create/Delete/Describe/Update/List), permissions (Put/Remove), connections (Create/Describe/Delete/List/Update/Deauthorize), API destinations (Create/Describe/Delete/List/Update), replays (Start/Describe/List/Cancel), endpoints, partner/SaaS event sources. Lambda target dispatch on PutEvents; S3 EventBridge notifications; archives capture matching events and StartReplay re-dispatches them in a background thread.
gotchas: SaaS/partner event source APIs are control-plane stubs — no real third-party integration
Connection authorization is stored but not used for actual API destination calls
Replay re-dispatches events in a background thread — timing is not guaranteed
TestEventPattern uses fnmatch-based matching, not the full AWS event pattern grammar

firehose.notes: 11 operations: CreateDeliveryStream, DeleteDeliveryStream, DescribeDeliveryStream, ListDeliveryStreams, PutRecord, PutRecordBatch, UpdateDestination, TagDeliveryStream, UntagDeliveryStream, ListTagsForDeliveryStream, StartDeliveryStreamEncryption, StopDeliveryStreamEncryption. Destinations: ExtendedS3, S3 (deprecated alias), HttpEndpoint. S3 destination records are written synchronously to the local S3 emulator. DeliveryStreamType=KinesisStreamAsSource is fully wired: records put into the source Kinesis stream are forwarded to the configured ExtendedS3 / S3 destination inline on PutRecord / PutRecords (same fan-out pattern as SNS→SQS), honoring Prefix and DeliveryStartTimestamp. ProcessingConfiguration.Processors[].Type=Lambda is invoked per batch with the AWS-shape event ({invocationId, deliveryStreamArn, region, records:[{recordId, approximateArrivalTimestamp, data(base64)}]}); response {records:[{recordId, result, data}]} with result Ok|Dropped|ProcessingFailed; Lambda failures pass records through unchanged (best-effort per AWS).
gotchas: HttpEndpoint destination buffers records in-memory — no actual HTTP delivery
S3 destination requires the target bucket to already exist in the S3 emulator
No buffering interval or size-based batching — S3 writes happen synchronously on each PutRecord

glue.notes: Full Data Catalog: databases, tables, partitions, connections, crawlers, jobs, job runs, security configurations, classifiers, partition indexes, crawler metrics, tags, triggers, workflows. Python shell jobs execute via subprocess. Spark jobs (glueetl/gluestreaming) run on the official amazon/aws-glue-libs PySpark image (GlueVersion 4.0 / 3.0) on MiniStack's Docker network. Override image via GLUE_DOCKER_IMAGE. Crawlers transition through RUNNING state with configurable timer (GLUE_CRAWLER_RUN_SECONDS).
gotchas: Spark jobs require Docker socket and pull the ~2GB amazon/aws-glue-libs image on first use
Python shell jobs run as local subprocesses — no isolation from the MiniStack process
Crawlers run a timer but do not actually crawl S3 data to infer schemas
Without Docker, Spark job runs will fail

iam.notes: 50+ actions: users, groups, roles, policies (managed + inline), access keys (Create/List/Delete/Update/GetLastUsed), instance profiles, service-linked roles, OIDC providers, attached/inline policies for users and roles, assume role policy updates, SimulatePrincipalPolicy, SimulateCustomPolicy, TagRole/UntagRole/ListRoleTags, TagUser/UntagUser/ListUserTags, TagPolicy/UntagPolicy/ListPolicyTags.
gotchas: No policy evaluation — policies are stored but never enforced on API calls
SimulatePrincipalPolicy/SimulateCustomPolicy return stub results
Access key rotation is tracked but credentials are not validated on requests

imds.notes: IMDSv1 + IMDSv2; default credential chain falls through to a ministack-instance-role document with ASIA* session creds. Point SDKs via AWS_EC2_METADATA_SERVICE_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4566. Set MINISTACK_IMDS_V2_REQUIRED=1 to require the token PUT.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — returns global credentials
Not persisted — tokens are in-process only
Credentials are synthetic — not tied to any real IAM role

inspector2.notes: 14 operations covering Enable/Disable/ListFindings/BatchGetFindingDetails/ListCoverage/ListCoverageStatistics/ListFindingAggregations/SearchVulnerabilities plus filter and tag CRUD. Deterministic stub vulnerability findings for ECR images, Lambda functions, and EC2 instances.
gotchas: Findings are deterministic stubs — no actual vulnerability scanning is performed
SearchVulnerabilities returns pre-defined stub results

iot.notes: AWS IoT Core: Things, ThingTypes, ThingGroups, certificates via local CA, IoT Policies with versioning, DescribeEndpoint. MQTT 3.1.1 over WebSocket on the gateway port + HTTP iot-data Publish. Persistent sessions, QoS 1 with DUP-flag retransmits, LWT, retained messages. Multi-tenant by account-prefixed topics. Local CA at GET /_ministack/iot/ca.pem. Requires cryptography package (ships in [full]).
gotchas: Requires the 'cryptography' Python package for certificate generation
MQTT broker is in-process — no external broker dependency
Certificate validation uses a local CA — not interchangeable with AWS IoT certificates
Topic prefixing is transparent but means raw MQTT clients must use account-prefixed topics

iot_data.notes: IoT Data Plane HTTP API (iot-data service). Publish operation bridges into the in-memory MQTT broker via the iot module. Routed by credential scope (iotdata) or host pattern (data-ats.iot.{region}.{host}).
gotchas: Only Publish is implemented — GetRetainedMessage/ListRetainedMessages are not yet available
No AccountScopedDict — delegates to the iot module for account scoping

kinesis.notes: 26 operations: CreateStream, DeleteStream, DescribeStream, DescribeStreamSummary, ListStreams, PutRecord, PutRecords, GetShardIterator, GetRecords, MergeShards, SplitShard, UpdateShardCount, ListShards, IncreaseStreamRetentionPeriod, DecreaseStreamRetentionPeriod, AddTagsToStream, RemoveTagsFromStream, ListTagsForStream, RegisterStreamConsumer, DeregisterStreamConsumer, ListStreamConsumers, DescribeStreamConsumer, StartStreamEncryption, StopStreamEncryption, EnableEnhancedMonitoring, DisableEnhancedMonitoring. Partition key to shard routing; AWS limits enforced (1 MB/record, 500 records/batch, 5 MB payload, 256-char partition key).
gotchas: Enhanced monitoring is stored but no actual CloudWatch metrics are emitted
Stream encryption is tracked as metadata but data is not actually encrypted
Consumer enhanced fan-out (SubscribeToShard) is not implemented

kms.notes: 8 operations: CreateKey, ListKeys, DescribeKey, Sign, Verify, Encrypt, Decrypt, GenerateDataKey, GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext. Uses the cryptography package for real RSA/EC key operations when available.
gotchas: Sign/Verify with real cryptographic operations requires the 'cryptography' package
Without cryptography, encryption uses simplified/stub operations
Key rotation is not implemented
Key policies are not stored or evaluated

lambda_svc.notes: 40+ operations: CreateFunction (now accepts DurableConfig), DeleteFunction, GetFunction, GetFunctionConfiguration, ListFunctions (paginated), Invoke (RequestResponse/Event/DryRun), UpdateFunctionCode, UpdateFunctionConfiguration, PublishVersion, ListVersionsByFunction, CreateAlias, GetAlias, UpdateAlias, DeleteAlias, ListAliases, AddPermission, RemovePermission, GetPolicy, ListTags, TagResource, UntagResource, PublishLayerVersion, GetLayerVersion, GetLayerVersionByArn, ListLayerVersions, DeleteLayerVersion, ListLayers, AddLayerVersionPermission, RemoveLayerVersionPermission, GetLayerVersionPolicy, CreateEventSourceMapping, DeleteEventSourceMapping, GetEventSourceMapping, ListEventSourceMappings, UpdateEventSourceMapping, PutFunctionConcurrency, GetFunctionConcurrency, DeleteFunctionConcurrency, CreateFunctionUrlConfig, GetFunctionUrlConfig, UpdateFunctionUrlConfig, DeleteFunctionUrlConfig, ListFunctionUrlConfigs. **Durable Functions (Durable Execution)** — CheckpointDurableExecution, GetDurableExecutionState, GetDurableExecution, GetDurableExecutionHistory, ListDurableExecutionsByFunction, StopDurableExecution, plus the three external callback ops (SendDurableExecutionCallbackSuccess, SendDurableExecutionCallbackFailure, SendDurableExecutionCallbackHeartbeat). Resume scheduler fires WAIT expiries, callback timeouts, and step-retry backoffs. State persists across restarts. Python and Node.js runtimes execute with warm worker pool; provided.al2023/provided.al2 runtimes execute via Docker RIE. Code via ZipFile, S3Bucket/S3Key, or ImageUri. SQS, Kinesis, and DynamoDB Streams event source mappings. Invoke LogResult returns user output + traceback on error. TracingConfig.Mode=Active injects _X_AMZN_TRACE_ID (Root=1-<8hex>-<24hex>;Parent=<16hex>;Sampled=1) into the runtime per invocation so the AWS X-Ray SDK works on the warm worker, provided runtime, and local subprocess executors.
gotchas: Python/Node.js run in-process by default — no container isolation unless using provided.* runtimes
provided.* runtimes (Go, Rust, C++) require Docker socket for RIE execution
Event source mappings poll in background threads — timing is best-effort
ImageUri-based functions require Docker to pull and run the image
Warm worker pool reuses processes — global state can leak between invocations
TracingConfig.Mode=Active is not supported on the docker RIE executor (AWS RIE drops X-Ray upstream) — logs a warning

lambda_durable.notes: AWS Lambda Durable Functions (Durable Execution) preview API (2025-12-01). 9 operations: CheckpointDurableExecution, GetDurableExecutionState, GetDurableExecution, GetDurableExecutionHistory, ListDurableExecutionsByFunction, StopDurableExecution, plus the three external callback ops SendDurableExecutionCallbackSuccess, SendDurableExecutionCallbackFailure, SendDurableExecutionCallbackHeartbeat. CreateFunction accepts DurableConfig. A resume scheduler fires WAIT expiries, callback timeouts (Callback.Timeout / Callback.Heartbeat), and step-retry backoffs (NextAttemptDelaySeconds). State persists across MiniStack restarts — the in-memory callback index is rebuilt from restored executions on boot and pending timers are re-armed. End-to-end verified against the official aws-durable-execution-sdk-python 1.5.0 and aws-durable-execution-sdk-java 2.44.13.
gotchas: Preview API — AWS may revise the wire shapes before GA
Step-retry depends on cold-start behavior; examples that store attempt counters in module-level state (count() from itertools) won't progress across MiniStack's cold-start retries

mediaconnect.notes: 5 operations: CreateFlow, DescribeFlow, ListFlows, UpdateFlow, ListTagsForResource. Routes under /v1/flows[/{FlowArn}] and /tags/{ResourceArn}. Control-plane-only stub — flow records are metadata, no real streaming or transcoding. ListFlows returns the AWS-shape ListedFlow projection (no Outputs/Sources/Entitlements). UpdateFlow is narrow to AWS-allowed top-level fields (SourceFailoverConfig, Maintenance, SourceMonitoringConfig, NdiConfig).
gotchas: No real flow streaming — flows are control-plane metadata only
Wire field names are camelCase per AWS REST-JSON; the in-memory record matches
Start/Stop/Pause/Resume flow lifecycle ops are out of scope; flows always read as STANDBY

mwaa.notes: 7 operations: CreateEnvironment, GetEnvironment, DeleteEnvironment, UpdateEnvironment, ListEnvironments, CreateWebLoginToken, CreateCliToken. Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow — real apache/airflow:<version> containers (2.x and 3.x), DAG sync from S3, InvokeRestApi proxy.
gotchas: Requires Docker socket for real Airflow container creation
DAG sync reads from the S3 emulator's DagS3Path — bucket must exist
Container startup is async — environment may take time to become AVAILABLE
CreateWebLoginToken/CreateCliToken return synthetic tokens

opensearch.notes: 11 operations: CreateDomain, DescribeDomain, DescribeDomains, DeleteDomain, ListDomainNames, UpdateDomainConfig, DescribeDomainConfig, DescribeDomainChangeProgress, ListVersions, GetCompatibleVersions, AddTags/ListTags/RemoveTags. Management plane on /2021-01-01/* (boto3.client('opensearch'), SigV4 scope es). Default data plane is a stub (<domain>.ministack.local:9200). Set OPENSEARCH_DATAPLANE=1 to spawn one real opensearchproject/opensearch container per CreateDomain. Add OPENSEARCH_DASHBOARDS=1 for a per-domain dashboards sidecar.
gotchas: Data plane is a stub endpoint by default — no actual Elasticsearch/OpenSearch queries
Real containers require Docker socket and OPENSEARCH_DATAPLANE=1
Domain creation is non-blocking — status transitions asynchronously
Access policies are stored but not enforced

organizations.notes: Single-master-account org auto-initialised per tenant. Nested OUs with Path field (2026-03-31 AWS additive change). FeatureSet=ALL. CreateAccount, DescribeAccount, ListAccounts, CreateOrganizationalUnit, ListOrganizationalUnitsForParent, DescribeOrganization, etc.
gotchas: Each tenant gets its own independent organization — no cross-account org structure
Created accounts are metadata-only — no real AWS account provisioning

pipes.notes: Minimal EventBridge Pipes for local CFN use. Source: DynamoDB Streams. Target: SNS. Lifecycle: create/delete via CloudFormation handlers. Background poller thread reads DynamoDB Stream records and publishes to SNS target.
gotchas: Only DynamoDB Streams source and SNS target are supported
Pipe is created and managed through CloudFormation handlers, not direct API calls
Background poller restarts on state restore for RUNNING pipes

rds.notes: CreateDBInstance spins up real Postgres/MySQL Docker container; returns actual host:port endpoint. Non-blocking create; daemon thread waits for container liveness, sets DBInstanceStatus to 'available' or 'failed'. PERSIST_STATE=1 respawns containers on boot.
gotchas: Requires Docker socket for real database container creation
Without Docker, instances are metadata-only stubs
Container startup is non-blocking — instance status transitions asynchronously
Database engine version selection maps to specific Docker image tags

rds_data.notes: RDS Data API; routes SQL to real Docker-backed RDS containers when present; supports MySQL (pymysql) and PostgreSQL (psycopg2). REST paths: /Execute, /BeginTransaction, /CommitTransaction, /RollbackTransaction, /BatchExecute. Surfaces DatabaseUnavailableException (504) when container-backed cluster isn't reachable.
gotchas: Requires pymysql (MySQL) or psycopg2 (PostgreSQL) Python packages for real SQL execution
Not in _state_map — no independent persistence
Falls back to in-memory stub when no Docker-backed RDS container is available

resource_groups.notes: 13 operations: CreateGroup, GetGroup, DeleteGroup, UpdateGroup, ListGroups, GetGroupQuery, UpdateGroupQuery, GetGroupConfiguration, PutGroupConfiguration, GroupResources, UngroupResources, ListGroupResources, ListGroupingStatuses, SearchResources, Tag, Untag, GetTags, GetAccountSettings, UpdateAccountSettings.
gotchas: Tag-sync operations are intentionally not implemented
SearchResources queries the in-memory tag state only

route53.notes: Hosted zones (Create/Get/Delete/List/ListByName/UpdateComment), record sets (ChangeResourceRecordSets/List), changes (GetChange), health checks (Create/Get/Delete/List/Update), tags (ChangeTagsForResource/ListTagsForResource). REST/XML API under /2013-04-01/.
gotchas: DNS records are metadata-only — no actual DNS resolution
Health checks are stored but never actually evaluated
GetChange always returns INSYNC — no propagation delay modeled

s3.notes: Full S3 implementation: CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, ListBuckets, HeadBucket, PutObject, GetObject, DeleteObject, HeadObject, CopyObject, ListObjectsV1/V2, DeleteObjects (batch), multipart upload (Create/UploadPart/Complete/Abort/List/ListParts), object tagging, ListObjectVersions, bucket sub-resources (Policy/Versioning/Encryption/Lifecycle/CORS/ACL/Tagging/Notification/Logging/Accelerate/RequestPayment/Website), Object Lock (retention/legal hold enforcement on delete), replication (Put/Get/Delete), range requests (206), Content-MD5 validation, encoding-type=url.
gotchas: Optional disk persistence via S3_PERSIST=1 or S3_DATA_DIR
ACLs are stored but not enforced on access
Bucket policies are stored but not evaluated
Lifecycle rules are stored but not automatically executed
Replication configuration is stored but objects are not actually replicated

s3files.notes: S3 disk-persistence helper module; no public ops. Internal helper for S3_PERSIST/S3_DATA_DIR functionality.
gotchas: Internal module — not a standalone AWS service

s3tables.notes: 14 of 30 botocore operations: table buckets (Create/List/Get/Delete), namespaces (Create/List/Get/Delete), Iceberg-format tables (Create/List/Get/Delete) + GetTableMetadataLocation / UpdateTableMetadataLocation. Embedded Iceberg REST catalog at /iceberg for Spark integration. Missing: policy CRUD (table-bucket + table), encryption CRUD, maintenance config CRUD, GetTableMaintenanceJobStatus, RenameTable.
gotchas: 16 operations are not yet implemented (policy, encryption, maintenance, rename)
Iceberg metadata is held in memory — no external metastore
Data files are stored in MiniStack's S3 service

scheduler.notes: 12 actions: CreateSchedule, GetSchedule, ListSchedules, UpdateSchedule, DeleteSchedule, CreateScheduleGroup, GetScheduleGroup, ListScheduleGroups, DeleteScheduleGroup, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource. Schedule groups with cascading deletes; rate(), cron(), at() expressions; group/prefix/state filters; CFN AWS::Scheduler::Schedule and ScheduleGroup supported.
gotchas: Schedules are stored but not actually triggered — no background scheduler execution
rate()/cron()/at() expressions are parsed for validation but not evaluated

secretsmanager.notes: 14 operations: CreateSecret, GetSecretValue, ListSecrets, DeleteSecret, RestoreSecret, UpdateSecret, DescribeSecret, PutSecretValue, UpdateSecretVersionStage, TagResource, UntagResource, ListSecretVersionIds, RotateSecret, GetRandomPassword, ReplicateSecretToRegions, PutResourcePolicy, GetResourcePolicy, DeleteResourcePolicy, ValidateResourcePolicy.
gotchas: RotateSecret stores the rotation config but does not invoke a Lambda rotation function
Resource policies are stored but not evaluated
ReplicateSecretToRegions is metadata-only — no cross-region replication

servicediscovery.notes: Cloud Map — namespaces, services, instance registration. Integrates with Route 53 for DNS record management.
gotchas: DNS records created via Cloud Map integration are metadata-only in the Route 53 emulator

ses.notes: 20+ v1 Query API actions: SendEmail, SendRawEmail, SendTemplatedEmail, SendBulkTemplatedEmail, VerifyEmailIdentity, VerifyEmailAddress, VerifyDomainIdentity, VerifyDomainDkim, ListIdentities, GetIdentityVerificationAttributes, DeleteIdentity, GetSendQuota, GetSendStatistics, ListVerifiedEmailAddresses, CreateConfigurationSet, DeleteConfigurationSet, DescribeConfigurationSet, ListConfigurationSets, CreateTemplate, GetTemplate, DeleteTemplate, ListTemplates, UpdateTemplate, GetIdentityDkimAttributes, SetIdentityNotificationTopic, SetIdentityFeedbackForwardingEnabled. Plus v2 REST endpoints under /v2/email/. All emails stored in-memory for test inspection. Send statistics aggregated into 15-minute buckets.
gotchas: Emails are stored in-memory, not actually sent (unless SMTP relay is configured)
All identities auto-verify immediately
Send quotas are not enforced

ses_v2.notes: 13 operations: SendEmail, CreateEmailIdentity, GetEmailIdentity, DeleteEmailIdentity, ListEmailIdentities, CreateConfigurationSet, GetConfigurationSet, DeleteConfigurationSet, ListConfigurationSets, GetAccount, ListSuppressedDestinations, PutAccountSuppressionAttributes, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource.
gotchas: Shares _sent_emails_list with ses v1 module
Emails are stored in-memory, not sent (unless SMTP relay is configured)
Identities auto-verify immediately

sns.notes: 18 operations: CreateTopic, DeleteTopic, ListTopics, GetTopicAttributes, SetTopicAttributes, Subscribe, Unsubscribe, ConfirmSubscription, ListSubscriptions, ListSubscriptionsByTopic, GetSubscriptionAttributes, SetSubscriptionAttributes, Publish, PublishBatch, ListTagsForResource, TagResource, UntagResource, CreatePlatformApplication, CreatePlatformEndpoint. SNS to SQS fanout delivery; SNS to Lambda fanout (synchronous invocation). FIFO topics with 5-minute deduplication, sequence numbers, content-based deduplication, and subscription validation.
gotchas: HTTP/HTTPS subscriptions are not actually called — messages are stored only
Platform applications and endpoints are metadata stubs
SMS delivery is not implemented

sqs.notes: 17 actions: CreateQueue, DeleteQueue, ListQueues, GetQueueUrl, GetQueueAttributes, SetQueueAttributes, PurgeQueue, SendMessage, ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage, ChangeMessageVisibility, ChangeMessageVisibilityBatch, SendMessageBatch, DeleteMessageBatch, ListQueueTags, TagQueue, UntagQueue. Both Query API and JSON protocol. FIFO queues with 5-minute deduplication, message-group ordering, one in-flight message per group. DLQ support with RedrivePolicy. Long polling (WaitTimeSeconds).
gotchas: Long polling blocks the request for up to WaitTimeSeconds — no push notification
No real message retention enforcement — messages are not automatically deleted after retention period
ApproximateNumberOfMessages may not be perfectly accurate during concurrent access

ssm.notes: 12 operations: PutParameter, GetParameter, GetParameters, GetParametersByPath, DeleteParameter, DeleteParameters, DescribeParameters, GetParameterHistory, LabelParameterVersion, AddTagsToResource, RemoveTagsFromResource, ListTagsForResource. Parameter Store supports String, SecureString, StringList types.
gotchas: SecureString values are stored in plaintext — no actual KMS encryption
Parameter policies (expiration, notification) are not enforced

stepfunctions.notes: 28+ operations: CreateStateMachine, DeleteStateMachine, DescribeStateMachine, UpdateStateMachine, ListStateMachines, StartExecution, StartSyncExecution, StopExecution, DescribeExecution, DescribeStateMachineForExecution, ListExecutions, GetExecutionHistory, SendTaskSuccess, SendTaskFailure, SendTaskHeartbeat, CreateActivity, DeleteActivity, DescribeActivity, ListActivities, GetActivityTask, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource, PublishStateMachineVersion, DeleteStateMachineVersion, ListStateMachineVersions, CreateStateMachineAlias, UpdateStateMachineAlias, DeleteStateMachineAlias, DescribeStateMachineAlias, ListStateMachineAliases. Full ASL interpreter: Pass/Task/Choice/Wait/Succeed/Fail/Map/Parallel; Retry/Catch; waitForTaskToken; Activities (worker pattern); TestState API with mock and inspectionLevel; SFN_MOCK_CONFIG for AWS SFN Local compatible mocks; intrinsic functions; nested startExecution.sync; JSONata standard library (~30 built-in functions).
gotchas: Executions run in background threads — not truly parallel for Map/Parallel states
Wait states use real time.sleep — long waits block the execution thread
Task states invoke Lambda when available; otherwise return the input as output
JSONata is available but JSONPath is the default query language

sts.notes: 6 actions: GetCallerIdentity, AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, GetSessionToken, GetAccessKeyInfo, GetWebIdentityToken. Shares IAM module's XML builders and credential generators. Signatures not validated.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — stateless service, no per-account isolation
Signatures are never validated — any credential is accepted
AssumeRole does not check trust policies
Session tokens are synthetic and not tied to real IAM state

tagging.notes: 5 operations: GetResources, GetTagKeys, GetTagValues, TagResources, UntagResources. Resource Groups Tagging API; cross-service tag aggregation by reading each service module's tag state directly.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — reads from other services' AccountScopedDict stores
Not in _state_map — no independent persistence (reads live service state)
Tag writes delegate to each service's own tag storage format

transfer.notes: Control-plane JSON API: CreateServer, DescribeServer, DeleteServer, ListServers, StartServer, StopServer, CreateUser, DescribeUser, DeleteUser, ListUsers, ImportSshPublicKey, DeleteSshPublicKey. Data-plane: real SFTP listener on :2222 (SFTP_PORT), key-authenticated, S3-backed virtual filesystem. SFTP_PORT_PER_SERVER=1 allocates per-server ports from SFTP_BASE_PORT.
gotchas: SFTP data plane requires paramiko Python package
SFTP writes buffer entire file in memory before PUT to S3
rename is implemented as copy + delete (S3 has no atomic rename)
Authentication matches SSH public key across all users and servers

waf.notes: 18 operations: CreateWebACL, GetWebACL, UpdateWebACL, DeleteWebACL, ListWebACLs, AssociateWebACL, DisassociateWebACL, GetWebACLForResource, ListResourcesForWebACL, CreateIPSet, GetIPSet, UpdateIPSet, DeleteIPSet, ListIPSets, CreateRuleGroup, GetRuleGroup, UpdateRuleGroup, DeleteRuleGroup, ListRuleGroups, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource, CheckCapacity, DescribeManagedRuleGroup.
gotchas: WAF rules are stored but never evaluated against incoming requests
CheckCapacity always returns a valid capacity — no limit enforcement
DescribeManagedRuleGroup returns stub rule descriptions

waf_v1.notes: Minimal WAF v1 stub — empty lists, valid ChangeToken. Covers both AWSWAF_20150824 (waf classic/global) and AWSWAF_Regional_20161128 (waf-regional) target prefixes. Use wafv2 for full features.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — returns empty stub responses for all accounts
No persistence — state is not saved
All list operations return empty results
ChangeToken is always valid but no rules can be created
